lines.text: I call this meeting to order. Welcome here, everyone. And at this time, I'd like to give the opening to Deputy Mayor, Councillor Michael Zwaagstra.

lines.speaker: Michael Zwaagstra
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Michael Zwaagstra (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Last Friday, together with other members of council, I had the privilege of attending the Mennonite Heritage Village gala. The guest speaker was none other than former Provence MP Jake Epp. Jake Epp hardly needs an introduction. Not only did he serve as Provencher MP from 1972 to 1993, but he also held high-profile cabinet positions such as National Health and Welfare, Indian Affairs and Northern Development, and Energy, Mines and Resources. Prior to becoming an MP, Epp served on Steinbach Town Council And was a high school history teacher. Simply put, the man is a living legend. When I heard that Epp would be speaking at the MHV Gala, I knew that I had to attend, and I was not disappointed. Epp started his speech by apologizing for his weak voice and said that he suspected that it had something to do with aging. That was a somewhat humorous understatement since Epp is 85 years old. However, while his voice might have been wavering, his insight and wisdom remained as sharp as ever. For the first part of his speech, Epp took his audience on a trip down memory lane. He spoke about growing up in Steinbach during the 1940s, when World War II was raging. Interestingly, Epp was born on September 1st, 1939, the same day that Germany invaded Poland and World War II began. Epp also talked about his past political activities. In 1958, when Epp was only 18 years old, he helped organize Prime Minister John Diefenbaker's first visit to Steinbach. One of his tasks consisted of clearing old tires from the venue so that it could be used for a huge political rally. In 1970, at the age of 31, Epp was elected to town council. Epp mentioned in his speech that Mayor A.D. Penner later appointed him Deputy Mayor. It wasn't too long after that that Epp ran for Parliament and became the first Mennonite to serve in the House of Commons. Epp also spoke about some of the people who had the most impact on his life. He mentioned that he appreciated the writings of Christian apologist Francis Schaeffer, particularly his book, How Then Should We Live? This is a book that's been meaningful to me as well, since Schaeffer did an excellent job of highlighting the importance of Christians getting involved in public affairs. It's important to remember that Epp broke new ground when he ran for Parliament in 1972. Many Mennonite churches strongly discouraged any form of political involvement. While others banned it entirely. No doubt Epp dealt with a lot of naysayers at the time. However, I think that Epp proved that it is possible for Christians to enter politics without sacrificing their personal faith or their ethics. Epp also mentioned that one of his heroes was former Prime Minister John Diefenbaker. Now, those who know me know that I too am a huge Diefenbaker fan. Not only do I own pretty much every book written about him, but I'm always on the lookout for any Diefenbaker paraphernalia. Sadly, I never had the chance to meet Diefenbaker myself, so it's always a treat for me to hear from someone who knew Diefenbaker personally. Epp said that it's important for everyone to have heroes. I agree. While Epp would no doubt shy away from thinking of himself as a hero, That's classic Mennonite humility. I have no problem saying that Jake Epp is one of mine. Epp is a great example of someone who went into politics for the right reasons, made a positive difference while there, and got out with his integrity intact. Jake Epp shared much wisdom at the MHV gala, and I'd be happy to listen to him again anytime. Thank you.

The property is located within the Steinbach Industrial Park with several properties zoned both M1 light industrial and M2 heavy industrial in and around the vicinity of the subject property. lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Certainly it's always tricky in these types of situations when we have a request for allowing retail in the industrial park. We do try to protect our industrial park because the reason the industrial park is developed is for the purpose of industry. But I believe this situation is unique and is even different than the previous application that had been made by Adults and Teen Challenge. And a couple of things that make it unique. One is that we're talking about repurposing an existing building. So we're not talking about building a new building. Rather, we're repurposing a building that is already there that was built according to the standards that were in place at the time. Also, this property would be used by Adults and Teen Challenge for, for their offices and such, which is an appropriate use in the industrial park. And then out of the 23,000 square feet in the building, which is the size now, approximately 10,000 square feet would be used for the retail sales. So that would be less than half. So that would be a portion of it. Because obviously the retail sales, the reason that Adult and Teen Challenge has that, it's to provide work for people who are in the program. That is the primary reason for it. It's not your traditional retail store. We're not talking about a Walmart-type store locating in the industrial park. Okay. And so because we're— because they're proposing to repurpose an existing building and because the retail is different than your normal retail, I'm comfortable approving this. The reason I'm not including the condition of upgrading the pipe is simply that it was already— the building has already been built. It's already there. And obviously the service level that was provided worked for the building and what was being done at the time. And I didn't hear anything in the response from staff that indicates that the service level doesn't work for the building as— for the use that's proposed. And so I do agree with the— and that's why I included in the motion that, yes, if we have the option of the conditional use expiring when the applicant ceases retail sales activity on the site, absolutely. That's a reasonable condition to put in place because the intent here is not for this to become a permanent retail location. It's an It's intended to be an accommodation to allow this particular charitable organization to have a portion of the building used for retail. And as long as that is what's continuing to happen, then the conditional use is fine. But of course, if the property is ever sold, they move to another spot and things change, then the conditional use expires. If we have that option, and as staff say, we can put that option there, then we should have that. So therefore, I would I move that we approve the conditional use as stipulated.

So it's a little bit of a change from where we normally go of not wanting to have retail in our industrial. But this also isn't primarily retail for the purpose of what they're needing. lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Seconded by Councillor Hiebert. Go ahead, Councillor Siemens.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is a 3rd reading, so we've had—

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: We've discussed this twice already, and it was approved at each step, and then it had to go to municipal board for approval, and they have approved it. So this is the final step in borrowing $7.5 million for the event centre project. I believe this is This is the last borrowing for it, and that'll— once this is paid off, potentially in 2030, then our— the event centre will be paid off. When we budgeted this initially, we had an interest rate of 7%. We actually got it for almost half of that, at 3.8% over a 5-year term, which is our normal borrowing. We're very fortunate that we were able to do that. That is part of our policy. Thank you. This, this is good news that we can do this, and it's better news that we can actually accomplish it in a 5-year term.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Thank you. Anything further, Councillor Hiebert?

lines.speaker: Bill Hiebert
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Bill Hiebert (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. This is the final step of borrowing for the event centre, and we've all seen the event centre, and it's a beautiful building. And to have interest rates at 3.8% is a pretty good interest rate. So no, I have no problem approving this. I think it's a good deal. Thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay, anything further, council? Anything closing?

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Aye.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Got 9E, we've got excavator licenses. Looking for a motion to approve on page 30. Councillor Penner, seconded by Councillor Hiebert. Any comments?

lines.speaker: Susan Penner
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Susan Penner (Councillor)
lines.text: It's just a routine thing we do, even though we're not exactly sure why it needs to be discussed.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further?

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor)
lines.text: Nothing further, thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Anything further of council? Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried. Are there any questions of council today? Any questions? Okay, seeing none, we'll move to correspondence petitions. We got 11A. This is FCM funding decision, the enhanced tree canopy coverage at the Southeast Event Centre. We were successful in getting a grant for the amount of $46,170 for planting trees On the events, yes.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Through you, Mr. Mayor, to administration, have these trees been planted already or are these for future plants?

lines.speaker: Troy Warkentin
lines.title: City Manager
lines.label: Troy Warkentin (City Manager)
lines.text: These will be for the plantings that are coming up with the east parking lot that is just being built this summer.

lines.speaker: Jac Siemens
lines.title: Councillor
lines.label: Jac Siemens (Councillor) [medium]
lines.text: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: Earl Funk
lines.title: Mayor
lines.label: Earl Funk (Mayor)
lines.text: Okay. So these are all new trees to be added to our canopy in the city. Council, how would you like to take this information? Okay. We've got 11B. This is a funding decision again. This is from FCM, climate risk assessment and the creation of a climate adaptive plan. So council, we've just received a letter letting us know that we've been approved for the grant up to $70,000. How would you like to bring Proceed, take his information at this time? Okay. And we've got 11C. This is the St. Rat-Roselle Watershed District. This is the minutes of May 20th, 2025. Page— it starts on page 35. Council, how would you like to proceed? Take his information? Please. Okay. Council, there's no other business. Looking for a motion to adjourn. Councillor Hiebert. Seconded by Councillor Stevens. Call for the question. All those in favor? Opposed? That is carried.
